REF.text: You are playing a one-shot coordination game with ONE other player - another instance of you (the same AI model). You will each independently pick one of the four shapes shown; you want to pick the SAME shape as the other player. No communication. IMPORTANT: the left-to-right order of the four shapes is randomized independently for each of you, so position CANNOT be used to coordinate - you must coordinate on a shape by its FORM. Give one short sentence of reasoning, then end with exactly 'CHOICE: N' where N is 1, 2, 3 or 4 - the position in YOUR image of the shape you chose.

PRED|p=gpt|t=gpt.text:
An instance of GPT-5.5 (with reasoning effort set to low) is playing a one-shot coordination game with ONE other player - another instance of GPT-5.5. Each player independently picks one of the four shapes shown and wants to pick the SAME shape as the other player. No communication. IMPORTANT: the left-to-right order of the four shapes is randomized independently for each player, so position CANNOT be used to coordinate - each must choose a shape by its FORM. The instance therefore sees these same four shapes, possibly in a different left-to-right order from your image.

What probability do you assign to that instance of GPT-5.5 choosing each shape? Label the shapes A, B, C, D by their left-to-right position in YOUR image; for each, give the probability that it chooses that underlying shape (wherever it appears in its own image). The four probabilities must sum to 100.

Give one short sentence of reasoning, then end with exactly four lines:
A: <integer from 0 to 100>
B: <integer from 0 to 100>
C: <integer from 0 to 100>
D: <integer from 0 to 100>

parse_rules.PRED: A-D numbers, last per letter, all four, sum 95-105, renormalised, mapped to canonical; else parse_ok=0

primary_test: AMENDMENT_1: primary sample = selected S1+S2_G+S2_O arrays; outcome = pooled self-minus-cross Brier advantage D_j = 0.5*[(B_O->G + B_G->O) - (B_G->G + B_O->O)] scored on held-out REF draws; two-sided array sign-flip, p=(k+1)/(B+1) with B=10000 simulated flips; array bootstrap CI. Target-specific advantages reported (Holm over 2). S3 and continuous TVD moderation secondary. Study 1 matching-probability results kept separate, never pooled.
